15.0.0.en: God spoke to Moses because he was the prophet, the leader of the people and the receiver of the Law, and likewise to Aaron because he was the high priest responsible for applying the Law.

15.1.0.en: The first case is the emission of semen from the organs of the man (he spits), whether continuously or emitted for a period and then stopping (being stopped up), and it may return to flowing again. These are the symptoms of the disease of the issue, whose sufferer is considered unclean. This signifies carelessness and lack of discipline.

15.2.0.en: The uncleanness is not limited to the one with the issue, but also everything he sits or lies on, whether a bed, seats or any physical thing, which also becomes unclean. This signifies the transmission of evil from the wicked person to those around him, so that we may keep away from everything that relates to sin or leads to it.

15.3.0.en: God warns against approaching the one with the issue or what belongs to him and what he uses, for all these things are unclean, and He specifies them as follows:

15.3.1.en: 1- The bed on which the one with the issue lies. The two signify laziness and carelessness.

15.3.2.en: 2- The furniture, that is, the seats and belongings on which the one with the issue sits.

15.3.3.en: 3- Whoever touches the body of the one with the issue --< signifies clinging to the unclean. The Law tries to keep us away from every appearance of uncleanness, so a person must care, by his own will, for his purity in all his dealings with those around him.

15.3.4.en: And if a person becomes unclean through any of the above, he must do the following:

15.3.5.en: 1- He washes his clothes, as a symbol of the cleansing of his conduct.

15.3.6.en: 2- He bathes, as a symbol of the purity of his inner being.

15.3.7.en: 3- He remains unclean until the evening, as a symbol of remembering the seriousness of uncleanness so as to guard against it. The unclean person refrains from eating of the peace offerings or taking part in the religious feasts so that he may be careful afterward, because the clean person enjoys drawing near to God in every way.

15.4.0.en: A clean person may be made unclean against his will when the one with the issue spits on him, whether he does not intend it or whether he is wicked and does it in contempt of this clean person. In both cases the clean person becomes unclean because unclean spittle fell on him. This signifies a warning against anything that comes from the unclean, for their words and deeds are unclean and must be avoided.

15.4.1.en: And the remedy, if this clean person becomes unclean, is that he do as in the previous cases, that is, wash his clothes, bathe, and remain unclean until the evening.

15.5.0.en: Likewise everything on which the one with the issue rides, whether an animal or any equipment placed on the animal such as the saddle (the packsaddle), is unclean, and everyone who touches or carries it becomes unclean. This signifies the use of the means of evil that the unclean use.

15.5.1.en: And the remedy is that the one who became unclean bathes, washes his clothes, and remains unclean until the evening.

15.6.0.en: The one with the issue must wash his hands before touching any person; if he does not do this and touches someone, he makes him unclean. This signifies clinging to the wicked.

15.6.1.en: And the remedy is that this unclean person washes his clothes, bathes, and remains unclean until the evening.

15.7.0.en: The vessels that the one with the issue touches become unclean, and they are of two kinds:

15.7.1.en: 1- Cheap vessels such as earthen vessels, which must be broken and disposed of.

15.7.2.en: 2- Expensive vessels such as those made of wood and metal, which are rinsed with water. This signifies that sin defiles the place and everything connected with the sinner, and that by washing, that is, repentance and prayer, everything is sanctified; but any physical thing that causes stumbling must be disposed of, such as unclean pictures or films.

15.8.0.en: The cleansing of the one with the issue is carried out in the following steps:

15.8.1.en: 1- Seven days must pass after the issue has stopped, to confirm that the issue will not return.

15.8.3.en: 3- He bathes, that is, washes his body in running water, that is, flowing water like the water of rivers, not pools or marshes.

15.9.0.en: The fourth step in the cleansing is done by the cleansed one with the issue seven days after the issue has stopped. He goes to the priest and offers two turtledoves or two young pigeons, that is, two small doves, because the meat of an old pigeon does not taste good and one must offer God the best; but the turtledove tastes good whether it is old or young. The priest kills one of them and burns it entirely on the altar, so it is a burnt offering, while the other he kills as a sin offering and the priest eats it (as mentioned in ch. 1:14-17). Thus the one with the issue completes his purification.

15.9.1.en: Take care not to cling to the wicked and all their places, their means of evil and their way of life, lest you be swept along with them into evil. And in proportion to your striving, be confident that God will support and protect you so that you keep your thoughts, your words and all your conduct in purity.

15.10.0.en: Seed of copulation: the emission of semen from the man, which by uniting with the ovum in the woman establishes seed or offspring. What is meant by copulation is that it takes place during sleep.

15.10.1.en: If a natural issue, not a diseased one, comes from the man when he is asleep, whether accompanied by dreams or not, he becomes unclean. This was so in the Old Testament because offspring or seed was born bearing the sin of Adam and Eve, before redemption was accomplished and we received salvation through Baptism. So the overflow of semen was considered unclean, and the one to whom this happened bathes all over and remains unclean until the evening.

15.11.0.en: Likewise every garment of cloth or leather on which a person is lying and on which this fluid falls becomes unclean and needs to be washed, and remains unclean until the evening.

15.12.0.en: The second natural case is the emission of semen in marital relations; the man and the woman must bathe and remain unclean until the evening.

15.12.1.en: In the New Testament, these natural things are no longer unclean, because redemption has been accomplished; but for the sake of propriety and cleanliness, washing is required, and Communion is not permitted, because these cases are considered a breaking of the fast, whether the emission of fluid is connected with evil dreams or with physical relations, so abstaining from such relations is required before Communion.

15.12.2.en: Physical relations within marriage are an expression of love and for the sake of begetting good offspring, but abstaining from them for the sake of Communion is good and necessary, because the aim of marriage is not sex; rather, it is a means of expressing love, and the spouses use it in the measure suitable for them and abstain from it for God's sake before Communion and during the fasts as much as they are able.

15.13.0.en: Here he speaks of the flow of blood from the woman's body in the case of the monthly period, which is the natural issue, and the woman is considered unclean for seven days. What is meant by seven days is a period sufficient for this flow to end, which usually lasts four or five days but does not exceed seven days. The woman is considered unclean in the Old Testament because the blood that comes out of her is connected with the production of the ovum, which unites with the sperm and produces offspring who bear the sin of Adam and Eve. In the New Testament it is not considered uncleanness, because Christ has accomplished redemption and gives us salvation in Baptism and the sacraments of the Church.

15.13.1.en: And everyone who touches the woman in her state of menstruation, that is, the flow of blood from her in the monthly period, becomes unclean.

15.14.0.en: Every bed on which this woman lies or place on which she sits during menstruation becomes unclean.

15.15.0.en: Everyone who touches the bed or belongings of the menstruating woman becomes unclean, and must bathe and remain unclean until the evening.

15.16.0.en: Here he refers to the things that are placed on the bed or on the seats on which the menstruating woman sits; these things become unclean by being placed on the bed or belongings, and whoever touches them becomes unclean until the evening. Here he affirms that uncleanness is transmitted from the unclean person to everything physical connected with her. And the one who touches these things does not need to bathe, because they were merely placed on the bed or belongings.

15.17.0.en: This is an unusual case, namely a husband lying with his wife while he does not know that she is menstruating, nor does she know either, that is, the flow of blood begins during or shortly before the marital relation, and this union took place unintentionally. The man too becomes unclean for seven days like the woman, and during the seven days in which he is unclean he makes unclean every bed on which he lies.

15.17.1.en: But if he knows that his wife is menstruating and lies with her deliberately, they are both cut off from the people of God for their carelessness, though they knew of the uncleanness, and for their boldness in having physical relations (ch. 20:18). All this signifies the importance of being scrupulous in keeping away from evil and uncleanness.

15.17.2.en: Although Christ has lifted the uncleanness from the woman in this period, yet for the sake of cleanliness and propriety it is not fitting for her to partake of the Holy Sacraments. Let this period be an opportunity for repentance over her sins, when she feels some pain and remembers God's judgment of old on Eve, pain in childbirth, a little of which appears during the monthly period. Let it be an opportunity for greater self-examination, prayer and reading of the Holy Bible, so that she may enjoy Christ who gave her salvation and purity.

15.18.0.en: Here he speaks of the flow of blood in a diseased manner, which is not limited to the flow of blood during the period of menstruation but extends for many days, or flows at other times than the period of menstruation; this makes the woman unclean. The diseased bleeding, that is, that which has no relation to menstruation, is considered uncleanness, because blood means life and its shedding signifies the death that came upon humanity after the fall into sin. But through the redemption of Christ the sentence of death was lifted, and consequently the uncleanness when blood flows; therefore a woman who bleeds because of a disease in the New Testament is considered clean, but she does not partake of the Holy Sacraments because of impropriety; yet in special cases, when the duration is long, she may partake with the guidance of the father of confession.

15.19.0.en: Because the woman with the issue is unclean, everything she lies or sits on becomes unclean.

15.20.0.en: Everyone who touches the woman with the issue, or what she sits or lies on, becomes unclean, and needs to bathe and remain unclean until the evening.

15.21.0.en: After the flow of blood stops, the woman waits seven days to be sure that the issue will not return again, and then she goes to the priest with two turtledoves or two small doves, and the priest offers one of them as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, and makes atonement for her, and she obtains her purity, as mentioned in the interpretation of (vv. 14, 15).

15.22.0.en: God commands Moses and Aaron to teach the people all these laws mentioned in this chapter, so that they may keep their purity and be able to draw near to the house of the Lord and His holy things, and so that they may be protected from death because of breaking the Law of God and falling into uncleanness.

15.23.0.en: Here he declares that this chapter contains the laws of cleansing for the woman and the man with an issue, of both kinds.

15.23.1.en: Use bodily weakness and sickness to humble yourself before God and ask for His help, and increase your prayers, readings and meditations, so that you may experience fellowship with Him in a new depth.

15.23.21.en: The Day of Atonement: general introduction:

15.23.22.en: The Day of Atonement is the greatest of the feasts of the Jews. On it atonement is made for the sins of the high priest and all his people and for everything in the tabernacle of the congregation. It signifies Good Friday, on which Christ offered atonement and salvation for the whole world, for everyone who believes in Him.

15.23.23.en: It is the only day on which a human being enters the Holy of Holies, namely the high priest, who signifies Christ, who by His redemption gave us salvation and brings us into the Kingdom of Heaven. On this day all the people fasted in humility over their sins, which God removes and for which He makes atonement by the sacrifices that signify Christ. And on this day the high priest takes off his splendid priestly garments and puts on the ordinary linen garments of the priests, so as to approach the service of this day in humility, just as Christ carried His Cross in humility on this day for our sake.

15.23.24.en: This feast falls on the tenth day of the seventh month, followed five days later, on the fifteenth day, by the Feast of Tabernacles. Because of the greatness of the Day of Atonement, it is called the Sabbath of Sabbaths, that is, complete rest. The chapter mentions the rites performed on this day, while the additional sacrifices offered on this day are mentioned in the Book of Numbers (ch. 29:7-11), and the duties performed by the people on this day are mentioned in (ch. 23:26-32). The rites particular to this feast are summarized in:

15.23.26.en: 1- The high priest leaves his dwelling and stays in a room next to the temple or in a tent beside the tabernacle of the congregation to prepare for the rites of the feast.

15.23.27.en: 2- The elders of the Sanhedrin, that is, the supreme council of the Jews, recite to him the rites of this feast throughout the seven days so that he may know them perfectly, because he will perform some of them alone inside the Holy of Holies.

15.23.28.en: 3- During these seven days the high priest carries out the priestly service in the tabernacle of the congregation, such as offering the sacrifices and lighting the lamps inside the sanctuary.

15.23.29.en: 4- On the night of the Day of Atonement the high priest does not sleep, and the priests stay around him so that he may be careful lest he have a dream by which his body would be made unclean.

15.23.30.en: b- The rites of the feast:

15.23.32.en: The first stage: the morning sacrifice (Ex 29:38-42, Num 28:3-8)

15.23.33.en: 1- The high priest bathes and puts on his splendid priestly garments (Ex 28).

15.23.34.en: 2- He commands the priests who assist him to remove the ashes from the bronze altar and clean it in preparation for the service of this great day.

15.23.35.en: 3- He slaughters and offers a lamb of the first year as a burnt offering, and with it one tenth of flour mingled with a fourth part of a hin of oil, and pours a fourth part of a hin of wine on the sacrifice (Ex 29:38-42), as is customary every morning in the tabernacle of the congregation. But the difference today is that the one who offers the morning sacrifice is the high priest himself, and it is doubled if the Day of Atonement falls on a Sabbath (Num 28:9, The second stage: the service of atonement:

15.23.36.en: This is the service particular to the Day of Atonement, in which the high priest enters the Holy of Holies four times, while on the rest of the days of the year he never enters it. The rites are summarized as follows:

15.23.37.en: 1- The high priest takes off his splendid priestly garments and washes, and then puts on priestly garments of linen like the rest of the priests (v. 4).

15.23.38.en: 2- He lays his hand on the head of the bull that will be slaughtered as an atonement for his sins and the sins of the priests, confessing his sins and theirs, for he is their representative.

15.23.39.en: 3- He casts lots on the two goats presented as an atonement for the people, so that one of them is offered as a sin offering and the other for Azazel (vv. 7, 8).

15.23.40.en: 4- He slaughters the bull at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation and puts its blood in a vessel inside the sanctuary.

15.23.41.en: 5- He takes the censer and the incense dish, fills his hands with incense, and enters the Holy of Holies for the first time. He places the censer on a stone inside the Holy of Holies and puts plenty of incense in it, so the place is filled with incense, which covers the Ark of the Covenant, so that the high priest does not see it and does not die, for because of the greatness of the Ark it is not right for anyone to see it (vv. 12, 13). He leaves the incense inside the Holy of Holies so that the cloud of incense continues to cover the Ark and its cover.

15.23.42.en: 6- He takes some of the blood of the bull and enters for the second time and sprinkles it on the cover of the Ark seven times, as an atonement for his sins and the sins of the priests (v. 14).

15.23.43.en: 7- He lays his hand on the goat of the sin offering and slaughters it at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, and puts its blood in a vessel inside the sanctuary.

15.23.44.en: 8- He enters for the third time into the Holy of Holies with the blood of the goat of the sin offering, offered for the sins of the people, and sprinkles some of it on the cover of the Ark seven times.

15.23.45.en: 9- He mixes the blood of the bull with the blood of the goat of the sin offering and sprinkles it on the contents of the sanctuary, then goes out from it and sprinkles it on the rest of the contents of the tabernacle of the congregation to make atonement for it (vv. 17-19).

15.23.46.en: 10- He gives the second goat, alive, to a man to let it go in the wilderness for Azazel (vv. 20-22).

15.23.47.en: 11- He commands that the bull and the goat of the sin offering be burned and their ashes cast outside the camp.

15.23.48.en: 12- He takes off his linen garments and washes, and then puts on his full priestly garments, that is, the splendid ones.

15.23.49.en: 13- He offers two rams as a burnt offering to God at the feast, one for himself and the other for the people.

15.23.50.en: The third stage: the additional sacrifices, which are mentioned in (Num 29:7-11), for himself and for the people, and which include:

15.23.51.en: 1- A bull as a burnt offering, and with it three tenths of fine flour mingled with oil and half a hin of wine, which he pours on it when offering it.

15.23.52.en: 2- A ram as a burnt offering, and with it two tenths of fine flour mingled with oil and a third of a hin of wine.

15.23.53.en: 3- Seven lambs of the first year as burnt offerings, and with each one of them one tenth of fine flour mingled with oil and a fourth part of a hin of wine.

15.23.54.en: 4- A kid of the goats as a sin offering.

15.23.55.en: The fourth stage: the evening sacrifice (Num 28:8), which is offered every evening by the same rite as the morning sacrifice mentioned in the first stage. The difference on this day is that the high priest is the one who offers it, not the priests.
